tasks.spec:
You are fixing ONE file plus adding ONE test in the OBE podcast repo at /mnt/d_drive/repos/podcast. Do NOT git commit, git push, open a PR, or touch any systemd unit. Do NOT send anything externally (no ssh to the VPS, no Telegram, no email). Do not load skills or call MCP/Apps. Subscription/OAuth engines only, zero API spend. Use PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 and PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX=/tmp for python invocations. Files you may change: scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh and a NEW tests/test_run_podcast_loop_resilience.py. Nothing else.

WHAT HAPPENED (executed evidence, 2026-07-24): all five OBE podcast loops -- health 07:17, guest-acquisition 08:23, referral-flywheel 08:41, booking-readiness 09:07, production-publish 10:13 -- were killed by systemd at their 40-minute TimeoutStartSec. The Codex worker task finished fine each time (receipts written ~4 minutes in). What hung was the SECOND Ringer task, the cross-model QA reviewer on engine 'opencode' with model zai-coding-plan/glm-5.2: zero output, timed out at 1200s, and Ringer's hardcoded max_attempts=2 (ringer.py line ~7043) ran it again for another 1200s. 2400s of reviewer on top of the worker blew the unit budget. Because `python3 $RINGER run` is a plain blocking call at scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh line ~294, systemd's SIGTERM killed bash before ANY line after it ran -- so the QA gate, the escalation delivery (line ~336-338) and the notify-failure accounting never happened. Zero .QA.md files exist for 2026-07-24; the last are from 2026-07-23. health-20260724.log logged 0 'telegram delivered' lines; health-20260723.log logged 2. Five real escalations (including 'pipeline is 2/6, Jul 30 queue empty, assign Fred's production owner') were written to disk and never reached the owner. The Z.AI lane is confirmed dead, not misconfigured: a bare `opencode run -m zai-coding-plan/glm-4.7 --format json 'Reply with exactly: LANE_OK'` produced no output in 90s and had to be killed; glm-5.1 and glm-5.2 behave identically; `opencode auth list` shows the Z.AI Coding Plan credential present and the CLI at v1.18.4 works.

THE CONTRACT YOU ARE IMPLEMENTING (owner decision, Ankit, 2026-07-24): a dead reviewer lane must NEVER be able to silence an escalation, and must never consume the whole unit budget. The reviewer moves to the Claude Max subscription lane.

MAKE EXACTLY THESE CHANGES to scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh. Every new environment variable must default to today's production behaviour when unset, and the script must keep working under `set -u`.
1. REVIEWER ENGINE: the global default becomes claude-lean -- QA_ENGINE="${LOOP_QA_ENGINE:-claude-lean}" (line ~49, currently opencode). The worker default stays codex, so worker and reviewer stay CROSS-MODEL by construction. Leave the production-publish case (line ~74) alone: it already overrides to codex against a claude-lean/opus worker, which is also cross-model and does not touch the dead lane. No other loop may default to opencode.
2. TEST SEAMS (test-only; identical production behaviour when unset):
   - RECEIPT_DIR="${LOOP_RECEIPT_DIR:-$REPO/episodes/_loop_receipts}"
   - RINGER="${LOOP_RINGER_BIN:-/home/ankit114/repos/ringer/ringer.py}"
   - LOOP_TELEGRAM_SINK: when set to a file path, the telegram() function MUST append the message to that file (a line of its own containing the message text) and return 0 WITHOUT any ssh, instead of the real VPS dispatch. When unset, the ssh path is byte-for-byte what it is today, including the two-attempt retry, the '"ok":true' proof, the ALERT-FAILED marker and TG_FAILED accounting.
   - LOOP_WORKER_TIMEOUT_S (default 1500) and LOOP_QA_TIMEOUT_S (default 420) feed the generated manifest's per-task timeout_s (currently hardcoded 2400 and 1200). Ringer retries a failed task once, so these defaults keep worst case inside the unit budget.
3. HARD RUN BUDGET: wrap the Ringer run so the script ALWAYS regains control. Use LOOP_RUN_BUDGET_S (default 2040, i.e. 34 minutes of the unit's 40) with `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=30s`. When the budget fires (exit 124 or 137), that is a FAILED run: notify with a message that names which artifacts exist (receipt present yes/no, QA verdict present yes/no) and says the run hit its budget, and exit non-zero.
4. ESCALATION CAN NEVER BE STRANDED:
   - add deliver_escalation_once(): if the escalation file exists and its marker file "${ESCALATE_FILE}.delivered" does not, send it through telegram() with the existing 'PODCAST <loop> LOOP - needs you:' framing and then create the marker. Exactly-once, idempotent.
   - call it as soon as the Ringer run returns and the escalation file exists -- BEFORE the QA verdict gate, so a reviewer failure cannot suppress it.
   - install a `trap` on EXIT, TERM and INT that calls deliver_escalation_once() and, when the run is ending abnormally, appends a short status line naming the reason (budget exceeded / signal received / reviewer unverified). The trap must be safe to run twice and must not turn a failed run into exit 0.
5. DO NOT WEAKEN THE GATE. Everything else stays: 'QA: PASS' is still the only success; REVISE still notifies; BLOCK and missing/unreadable verdicts still notify AND exit non-zero; the referral-flywheel post-QA automation still runs ONLY under QA: PASS with all of its existing artifacts and checks; a failed Telegram delivery still fails the run (TG_FAILED). If your change makes any of those pass more easily than before, you have broken the department's deny-by-default rule and the fix is wrong.

ADD tests/test_run_podcast_loop_resilience.py -- pytest, no network, no real ssh, no real Ringer. It must drive the real scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh with `bash` and a STUB ringer script (written into tmp_path, invoked through LOOP_RINGER_BIN, which must answer the `lint` subcommand with exit 0) plus LOOP_RECEIPT_DIR=tmp_path and LOOP_TELEGRAM_SINK=tmp_path/sink.txt. Cover at minimum: (a) HUNG REVIEWER -- the stub writes the receipt and the escalation file then sleeps far past LOOP_RUN_BUDGET_S=5; assert the runner returns on its own well inside the test's own timeout, exits non-zero, and the escalation text is in the sink; (b) HAPPY PATH -- the stub writes receipt + escalation + a 'QA: PASS' QA file and exits 0; assert exit 0 and the escalation appears EXACTLY ONCE in the sink (proving the trap does not double-send); (c) NO VERDICT -- the stub writes only the receipt; assert the runner exits non-zero (the gate still denies). Use the 'health' loop so no referral preflight runs. Keep the whole test file under a couple of minutes of wall clock.

VERIFY BEFORE YOU FINISH, and paste the real output into your final message: `bash -n scripts/run_podcast_loop.sh`, then `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_run_podcast_loop_resilience.py tests/test_run_podcast_loop_referral_automation.py -q -p no:cacheprovider`. A claim without that output is not done. Leave the working tree dirty -- the coordinator lands it.
tasks.verified: An independent stub-Ringer harness proves the runner now regains control from a hung reviewer inside its budget, still delivers the worker's escalation to the notify sink exactly once, still exits non-zero on a missing QA verdict, and still passes the repo's own runner tests -- i.e. the 2026-07-24 silent-failure mode is closed without loosening the deny-by-default QA gate
